result.question: I want to know whether the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at site MAIN is heading into trouble over the next couple of days, not just whether it looks bad today. Using the co and co2 samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, first check both series for gaps and tell me how many usable samples each has. Then try at least two forecasting models on co, including a simple last-value baseline, and backtest them on the final held-out sample. Give me each model's error and pick the one with the lowest error. Only prefer a pretrained model over the baseline if its error is at least 10% lower. Use the chosen approach to forecast co and co2 two days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% prediction interval for each day. From those forecasts, work out the projected CO2/CO ratio for each day. If the projected ratio drops below 3 on either day, treat it as likely paper involvement in a fault, tell me which day, and recommend an insulation check plus a confirmatory oil sample. If it stays between 3 and 10, call it normal and say no action is needed. If it goes above 10, flag general cellulose ageing for the next routine review. If co2 has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't forecast the ratio. Forecast co alone and flag any day where its upper bound is more than 20% above the latest co reading, and say that the ratio test couldn't be done. If co itself has fewer than 4 usable samples, skip the models and report only the first-to-last change in co per day as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
**Result: the paper insulation is not heading into a fault in the next two days. The projected CO2/CO ratio is about 41 on both days, which is above 10, so by your rules this goes on the next routine review as general cellulose ageing.**

**How I ran this:** the forecasting tools need a data file, and I had no way to create one from the sensor readings. My one attempt to point them at the readings directly was rejected. So I did all the modelling by hand, and I could not run a pretrained model at all. The results below are simple statistical models worked out manually.

**1. Gaps and usable samples** (daily readings, Jan 15 to 18)

| Date | co (ppm) | co2 (ppm) |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 |

- co has 4 usable samples and co2 has 4, with no gaps or missing values.
- Both meet the minimum of 4, so I ran the models and the ratio test.

**2. Backtest on co** (trained on Jan 15–17, tested on the held-out Jan 18 value of 33)

| Model | Forecast | Absolute error |
|---|---|---|
| Last value (baseline) | 35.0 | 2.00 |
| Straight-line trend | 36.5 | 3.50 |
| Average of past values | 32.33 | **0.67** |

- The average model has the lowest error. It isn't pretrained, so your 10% rule doesn't apply, and I chose it.
- A backtest on a single held-out sample is a weak basis for comparing models.

**3. Two-day forecasts with 80% intervals** (all four samples; interval based on how much the readings vary)

| Day | co (ppm) | co 80% interval | co2 (ppm) | co2 80% interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-19 | 32.5 | 28.7 – 36.3 | 1329.8 | 1288.5 – 1371.0 |
| 2024-01-20 | 32.5 | 28.7 – 36.3 | 1329.8 | 1288.5 – 1371.0 |

The average model predicts the same value every day, so both days are identical.

**4. Projected CO2/CO ratio**

- Day 1 (2024-01-19): about 40.9.
- Day 2 (2024-01-20): about 40.9.
- Even combining the interval ends the least favourable way, the ratio stays between about 35 and 48.
- It does not drop below 3 on either day, so there are no signs of paper involvement in a fault.
- It does not sit in the 3–10 normal band either.

**Recommendation:** no insulation check or extra oil sample is needed now. Flag general cellulose ageing for the next routine review. CO itself is steady and low at about 30–35 ppm.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved co and co2 for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window via iot.history and its manual sample counts (4 each, no gaps) and arithmetic (backtest errors, mean forecast 32.5/1329.75, ratio ~40.9 -> >10 cellulose ageing flag) are consistent with the data. However, it did not execute the expected pipeline: tsfm.data_quality failed on an 'iot://' path and was not retried with a proper dataset handle, tsfm.find_models was never called, no pretrained/catalog model was backtested against the naive last-value baseline (so the 10% preference rule could not actually be applied), and tsfm.run_recipe was never used to produce the two-step forecasts or calibrated 80% prediction intervals. The intervals and model comparison were hand-computed ad hoc rather than produced by the forecasting tooling the task required. The agent was transparent about these gaps, so this is not a hallucination, but the task is only partially complete. To fix: materialize the retrieved observations into a dataset the tsfm tools accept, run tsfm.data_quality on both channels, shortlist models with tsfm.find_models, run tsfm.run_recipe backtests (naive last-value plus at least one catalog model, fh=[1], holdout last sample), apply the 10% rule, then run tsfm.run_recipe with fh=[1,2] and conformal coverage 0.8 for co and co2, and compute the ratio from those outputs.
